descriptionChirho: A robber, bandit, or brigand; one who takes property by violence, as distinct from a mere thief (kleptes) who operates by stealth. In the NT used of the temple courts turned into a 'den of robbers' (Matt 21:13, Mark 11:17, Luke 19:46 leston), of the arrest of Jesus ('have you come out as against a robber?' Matt 26:55, Mark 14:48, Luke 22:52 lesten), of the two criminals crucified with Jesus (Matt 27:38, 27:44, Mark 15:27 lestai/lestas), of Barabbas identified as a robber (John 18:40 lestes), of the man who fell among robbers on the road to Jericho (Luke 10:30, 10:36 lestais/lestas), of those who climb into the sheepfold another way being thieves and robbers (John 10:1, 10:8 lestes/lestai), of Paul's dangers from robbers (2 Cor 11:26 leston). Uniform across languages: Hebrew shoded/listim, Arabic liss/lusus, German Rauber, French brigand, Korean gangdo, Hindi daku, Spanish ladron/salteador.
